title: Rigveda 7.85: To Indra and Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.85: To Indra and Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.85 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Indra and Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 545v-546r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.85.1-5 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 6, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 546r
translation.original_text:
1pu̱nī̱ṣe vā̍m ara̱kṣasa̍m manī̱ṣāṁ soma̱m indrā̍ya̱ varu̍ṇāya̱ juhva̍t | ghṛ̱tapra̍tīkām u̱ṣasa̱ṁ na de̱vīṁ tā no̱ yāma̍nn uruṣyatām a̱bhīke̍ ||
2spardha̍nte̱ vā u̍ deva̱hūye̱ atra̱ yeṣu̍ dhva̱jeṣu̍ di̱dyava̱ḥ pata̍nti | yu̱vaṁ tām̐ i̍ndrāvaruṇāv a̱mitrā̍n ha̱tam parā̍ca̱ḥ śarvā̱ viṣū̍caḥ ||
3āpa̍ś ci̱d dhi svaya̍śasa̱ḥ sada̍ḥsu de̱vīr indra̱ṁ varu̍ṇaṁ de̱vatā̱ dhuḥ | kṛ̱ṣṭīr a̱nyo dhā̱raya̍ti̱ pravi̍ktā vṛ̱trāṇy a̱nyo a̍pra̱tīni̍ hanti ||
4sa su̱kratu̍r ṛta̱cid a̍stu̱ hotā̱ ya ā̍ditya̱ śava̍sā vā̱ṁ nama̍svān | ā̱va̱varta̱d ava̍se vāṁ ha̱viṣmā̱n asa̱d it sa su̍vi̱tāya̱ praya̍svān ||
5i̱yam indra̱ṁ varu̍ṇam aṣṭa me̱ gīḥ prāva̍t to̱ke tana̍ye̱ tūtu̍jānā | su̱ratnā̍so de̱vavī̍tiṁ gamema yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text:
1FOR you I deck a harmless hymn, presenting the Soma juice to Varuṇa and Indra- A hymn that shines like heavenly Dawn with fatness. May they be near us on the march and guard us.
2Here where the arrows fall amid the banners both hosts invoke the Gods in emulation. O Indra-Varuṇa, smite back those-our foemen,yea, smite them withyour shaft to every quarter.
3Self-lucid in their seats, e'en heavenly Waters endowed with Godhead Varuṇa and Indra. One of these holds the folk distinct and sundered, the Other smites and slays resistless foemen.
4Wise be the priest and skilled in Law Eternal, who with his sacred gifts and oration. Brings you to aid us with your might, Âdityas: let him have viands to promote his welfare.
5May this my song reach Varuṇa and Indra, and, strongly urging, win me sons and offspring. To the Gods' banquet may we go with riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods with blessings.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 546r (numbered 67r by the scribe) (OPenn image 546, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.85.1 ‹-punīṣe vām arakṣasam manīṣām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 546v (numbered 67v by the scribe), begins in RV 7.86.2 ‹kadā mṛḷīkam su-manāḥ abhi›. Verses 7.85.1-5 end on this page; 7.85.1 begins on fol. 545v (numbered 66v by the scribe).
